1640.reason: The consumer library's existing stream-processing operation is widened so one application can handle several streams, with the list adjustable at runtime.

1641.reason: A forwarding session's connection concurrency rises from one to many, which is a limit and performance change with no new control.

1677.reason: Routine quarterly JDK refresh, but it also adds a newer TLS protocol to one line and a production-ready alternative garbage collector to another.

1754.reason: Existing drivers are relicensed as open source and gain incremental parameters, authentication options and data-library compatibility; the text treats both drivers as already existing.

1813.reason: The text presents a doubling of the cluster storage ceiling, although it applies only to the named government regions.

1882.reason: A deployable reference template assembled from existing services, not a change to any service's own functionality.

1906.reason: The existing sign-in gains a federated option through corporate identity providers via an AWS identity service.

1915.reason: Mixed point release; the instance type and operating system are catalogue additions, while the cluster metrics dashboard is a new monitoring interface.

1944.reason: A dedicated command-line tool giving the container service an application-centric build, release and operate workflow reaches 1.0; the text lists no changes from earlier versions.

2015.reason: A newer framework release joins the list of supported porting targets, which is a runtime version catalogue addition.

2047.reason: Essentially a restructuring of provisioned IOPS rates; the higher-performance volume preview is mentioned only as context for its pricing tier.

2063.reason: Preview of a re-engineered serverless database generation with fine-grained near-instant scaling and the full engine feature set, a substantially changed operating model.

2112.reason: Existing search ranking now adapts automatically from user behaviour and feedback, with no new interface or operation exposed.

2172.reason: Preview of a subsystem that generates managed, no-code web applications with their own corporate sign-in, so end users can monitor and act on device fleets outside the console.

2187.reason: A data-source plugin makes an external dashboard tool one more place to visualise data the service already exposes.

2188.reason: A new application-centric console view inside the operations suite, mainly aggregating existing operational data and runbooks.

2190.reason: A new visual server administration interface inside the operations suite, positioned as one more capability of it and not as a new operating model.

2210.reason: The storage location for new connection credentials moves by default into the customer's own account; there is no new option or operation.

2221.reason: Sellers of container listings get a self-service version and listing update flow, plus marketplace-hosted repositories they can push artifacts to directly.

2230.reason: The existing service link gains a private routing option through a customer VPC and dedicated connection instead of public endpoints.

2238.reason: One more operating system image joins those supported on the edge devices, a catalogue addition.

2265.reason: A deployable reference architecture aimed at compliance baselines, not a change to any AWS service.

2266.reason: An open source reference implementation built on existing services and published as a solution, not a managed offering or a service change.

2278.reason: Restore-to-a-moment recovery is extended to one more database engine on the on-premises deployment variant.

2291.reason: Two added pipeline action types make stack sets a further deployment target alongside the existing template deployment actions.
